name: Base pair
oneLine: Two letters that fit together: A with U, G with C.
howItWorks: Matching bases stick through weak bonds, like tiny magnets. G and C hold tighter than A and U. Heat shakes these bonds apart.
deeper: G–C pairs share three hydrogen bonds, A–U pairs two. Stacking between neighbouring pairs adds much of the real stability.
sizeComparison: a 50,000th the width of a hair
simplification: We only show the standard pairs. Real RNA also makes looser G–U pairs.
